steps.headline: Only offers worth your time
steps.body: Rounds screens every offer against Maya’s licenses, rate floor and calendar before it reaches her. The feed shows what passed, and each card says how the rate compares with the market.

metric.small: offers read per day; the agent hides 9 that break your rules

steps.name: 1.2.1 Discover

steps.headline: The real rate, not the posted one
steps.body: Pay is shown as take-home after the 3% fee, next to schedule, call and requirements. Risky terms are flagged before Maya commits to anything.

metric.small: take-home per hour after the 3% fee

steps.name: 2.1.1 Offer · Locum

steps.headline: Know your leverage before you ask
steps.body: A market histogram shows where the offer sits. The agent explains its recommendation in plain language — Maya can take it, change it or ignore it.
steps.name: 2.1.2 Offer · Agent analysis

steps.headline: Approve once. The agent negotiates.
steps.body: Maya picks which asks to send and adds a personal note. With a new facility nothing goes out without her approval.

metric.small: from offer to a signed term sheet

steps.name: 2.2.1 Review offer · First time

steps.headline: Sent. Now it’s the agent’s job.
steps.body: A clear status, an expected reply time and nothing to chase. If St. Mary’s goes quiet, the agent follows up on its own.
steps.name: 2.2.4 Confirmation · Counter sent

steps.headline: Negotiation, translated
steps.body: St. Mary’s accepted two of four asks. Instead of a redlined PDF, Maya sees what changed and the agent’s next move.
steps.name: 2.3.6 Facility response · Round 2

steps.headline: A term sheet a human can read
steps.body: Rate, schedule, cancellation, malpractice and non-compete — every term marked agreed, changed or flagged, with the take-home on top.
steps.name: 2.3.7 Term sheet · Ready to sign

steps.headline: Signed in a glance
steps.body: Face ID signs the exact term sheet Maya just read. If the facility’s contract later differs, the agent flags every mismatch.
steps.name: 2.3.11 Sign with Face ID

steps.headline: Booked, and the next steps are moving
steps.body: Signing starts credentialing with documents Maya already has. She sees what is done, what is next and who owns it.

metric.small: from offer to a signed term sheet

steps.name: 2.3.8 Term sheet · Signed

steps.headline: Credentialing without the chase
steps.body: Hospitals can take 30–120 days to credential a new locum, mostly waiting on paperwork. Rounds sends what’s already in the wallet and shows who is waiting on whom.
steps.name: 3.1.1 Credentialing · Tracker

steps.headline: All your work, one calendar
steps.body: Assignments from every facility and agency in one list — conflicts caught before they happen, timesheets a tap away.
steps.name: 3.2.1 Assignments

steps.headline: One inbox, agent included
steps.body: The agent’s thread sits next to every facility conversation. Anything that needs Maya rises to the top.
steps.name: 4.3.1 Inbox

steps.headline: Ask in plain language
steps.body: Offers, term changes and calendar moves come back as cards Maya can open or confirm in one tap.
steps.name: 4.3.2 Agent chat

steps.headline: The agent works in the open
steps.body: It says what it’s checking and how long it will take. Every action leaves a trace Maya can read back later.
steps.name: 4.3.6 Agent is working

steps.headline: Facilities talk to Maya, not around her
steps.body: Recruiters write in the same thread. The agent drafts replies and keeps a record of what was agreed — Maya decides what is sent.
steps.name: 4.3.3 Facility thread

steps.headline: Documents shared on purpose
steps.body: When a facility asks for a document, the agent finds it in the wallet and asks before sharing — with one facility only, revocable anytime.
steps.name: 4.3.7 Document requested in thread
